analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation: one new row in docs/reference/configuration.md at head line 329 for `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP`. The row describes a load-time shape warmup for ordinary EngineV2 slots. A 128-token shader-cache probe runs twice, and only a cold cache runs the shape cells, within 20 seconds per engine. It trains no rate or counter, and it is forwarded to the LaunchAgent. No code or controls changed in the supplied evidence. The rest of both units appears unchanged and I did not treat it as new behavior.

Security relevance is low. The documented variable is an operator-set environment toggle on the provider process, within the existing TB-003 operator trust model. It carries no secrets, keys, tokens or attestation material, and it does not alter App Attest, the coordinator contract, prefix-cache storage (T-041) or encryption. The warmup uses a synthetic 128-token probe, so I see no consumer plaintext (A-001) reaching it from the doc. I found no indication of persisted prompt-derived data or timing-oracle changes. T-041 and SEC-035 concern prefix-cache hit/miss TTFT, and a load-time warmup that is not part of request serving does not obviously widen that channel.

Open integration questions, not findings: the actual implementation in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift and the LaunchAgent passthrough list were not supplied. I cannot verify that the warmup uses only synthetic inputs, that the `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP` passthrough is really present, or that the 20-second bound holds. Any shape-warmup cache could in principle leave artifacts, but that is unverified from this doc-only change. A reviewer of the code-bearing PR should confirm these points. No threat-model regression is identified from this doc diff.
